description: odoo-ai-agents hooks - SessionStart readiness probe + browser-MCP permission self-apply + state-root planning-permission self-apply + ETHOS @import injector + guarded legacy-state-root migration + UserPromptSubmit intent detector + SubagentStop grounding enforcement & continuation nudge & resource-teardown gate & terminal-status telemetry + PreToolUse delegate reminder & coordinator source-write deny & unowned-lease-mutation deny & live-lease handback deny & capture-outside-state-root deny + Stop continuation nudge & browser-teardown advisory + PermissionDenied refused-give-back advisory + SessionEnd allocator gc crash-backstop. The SessionEnd hook only SPAWNS a detached worker and returns in milliseconds, so its `timeout` here bounds that spawn ONLY - the reaping's real bounds live in the script, because a SessionEnd hook is aborted once the batch's other hooks finish regardless of the timeout declared here (see the script's own header for the measurement). The drive-to-done and browser-teardown hooks are ADVISORY (never hard-block; parse-continuation.sh in particular has a HARD CONTRACT to never block - see its own header). There are exactly FOUR PreToolUse hard denies, each matcher-scoped and each refusing one shape. (1) block-coordinator-code-write.sh, matcher-scoped to Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|Bash, refuses production-source authoring by an agent the agent-role SSOT declares role=coordinator or role=spawner, Bash-mediated writes included (redirect, tee, sed -i, dd, cp/mv, git apply/patch, interpreter one-liners), because a gate that skipped Bash would look enforcing while the breach walked past it. The two command-parsing denies, block-coordinator-code-write.sh and block-unowned-lease-mutation.sh, segment the command through the shared SSOT hooks/command-segments.sh, which joins `\`-continued lines BEFORE splitting on `|| && ; | &` and drops a DATA heredoc's body: without the join a two-line `cp x.py dst.py` matched no detector at all, and without the body drop an agent appending a worklog entry that merely NAMED a source path was refused for writing it. (2) block-unowned-lease-mutation.sh, matcher-scoped to Bash plus the odoo-local lease_release / lease_park / lease_adopt tools, refuses a SUBAGENT's `allocator.py release` that names no owner (no --run-id / --session anywhere in that LOGICAL command - a flag on a `\`-continuation line counts, and used to not) or `allocator.py park` / `allocator.py adopt` that names no owner, any --force / --force-forget / reap-orphans --yes / acquire --allow-unowned override, and any APPLYING `allocator.py gc` (no --dry-run - the registry is machine-global, so a dispatch never reclaims across every session on the host) from a subagent, including inside `eval` and `$(...)` / backtick command substitutions, which the shell executes - the enforcement half of the allocator ownership guard, after a dispatch with a documentary brief released a live lease it had never acquired and destroyed the database. It is deliberately identity-free rather than keyed on a per-agent allow-list, because the agents that legitimately drive the allocator sit on both sides of the role line; acquire, bind, resume, heartbeat, gc --dry-run and a list-only reap-orphans are never refused. Its fourth arm closes the hole the owner-naming arm cannot: ownership is RUN-scoped and a forwarded INSTANCE_HANDLE carries the provider's run_id, so a consumer could name a real owner and destroy the provider's instance - a SUBAGENT's release, park or adopt (Bash or MCP) is therefore refused unless its target token appears in the caller's OWN transcript as a lease it obtained (the same correlation as the teardown gate, in the shared sourced hooks/lease-correlation.sh, so every lease that gate orders released passes here) or one a child it dispatched handed back UP (an adopt may also take a token its own lease_find returned - the resume-in-a-new-session path); a token that arrived in its brief is refused as forwarded. It fails open when that transcript cannot be read. The headers of (1) and (2) state the residuals they provably cannot catch. (3) block-handback-with-live-lease.sh, matcher-scoped to SubagentHandback, refuses a SUBAGENT's report hand-back while a lease it obtained itself is still LIVE and non-shared per the allocator's verdict and the handed-back message's closed continuation block does not forward THAT lease - an INSTANCE_HANDLE carrying its own lease_token in next.inputs; forwarding one lease's handle never clears a second one - status-blind, the same three exits and the same check as the SubagentStop teardown gate (the shared sourced hooks/teardown-check.sh, hooks/final-report.sh and hooks/lease-correlation.sh), because SubagentHandback delivers the report to the caller the moment it runs, before SubagentStop, so the SubagentStop block alone arrived after the caller already held a report whose lease was never given back; a denied SubagentHandback delivers nothing, and the agent calls it again once it has released, parked or forwarded the lease. It fails open on any uncertainty. (4) block-capture-outside-state-root.sh, matcher-scoped to this plugin's browser families (mcp__plugin_odoo-ai-agents_ and bare mcp__ forms of chrome-devtools|playwright|pagecast, each optionally -headed), refuses a browser capture whose write destination (filePath / filename / outputDirPath / webmPath / requestFilePath / responseFilePath) is relative or outside the capture area - <state root>/projects plus the ODOO_AI_PROJECT_DIR / ODOO_AI_WORKTREE_DIR override dirs a family can write (scripts/lib/browser_mcp_servers.py allowed_roots, the decision in scripts/lib/capture_paths.py), never the rest of the state root, which holds the lease registry, because a relative destination lands in the session's working directory - the repository - and the servers accept it; it denies only when the answering server provably carries its state-root flag (the bundled chrome-devtools started by scripts/mcp/browser_mcp_launch.py, or an opt-in family whose answering Claude registration - local, else project, else user scope - carries the flag) and otherwise allows the call with an advisory to re-run /odoo-ai-agents:odoo-setup browser, never refuses a tool that only reads a path or a call with no destination, and fails open on any uncertainty. Agent dispatch itself is NEVER denied at any depth: a subagent may launch its own children (that is how odoo-coding -> odoo-coder -> teammates runs), and the launcher collects each child's result per snippets/spawner-completion-contract.md R0 - inside its own turn when its agent-launch tool carries run_in_background, on a wake after it ends its turn when it does not. No other tool is ever denied - SubagentHandback only while the lease above is held, a browser capture only while its destination is outside the capture area (Bash with run_in_background: true stays free - a subagent may background a long command and wait for it inside the same turn, and only the TURN END with that command still running is refused, by enforce-background-wait.sh below; Odoo builds do not need it, they launch through the odoo-local instance_build tool, whose job_id job_wait blocks on), and the hook fails open on any unreadable payload. Its sibling remind-delegate.sh is unchanged and stays ADVISORY-only, always emitting the no-opinion value 'defer'. There are THREE SubagentStop hard blocks, all narrow and all scoped to the subagent only (never main): (1) the instance-teardown gate, which fires only on a live, non-shared lease that the SUBAGENT ITSELF obtained - correlated by the lease TOKENS its OWN transcript (agent_transcript_path, never the session-wide transcript_path) shows its own acquire / adopt calls receiving - never a forwarded token it merely served or resumed, and never by an acquisition-time window - never by the run id it shares with its parent and siblings, and judged live by the allocator's own `list --with-verdict` rather than a copied liveness rule - at a turn end whose REPORT - the message of a delivered SubagentHandback, else the final message (the payload's last_assistant_message, since the transcript file may not hold it yet) - does not forward THAT lease (an INSTANCE_HANDLE carrying its own lease_token in the fence's next.inputs - per lease, never one handle for all). Once a report was DELIVERED through SubagentHandback it is final, so this block then offers only release or park, never the handoff or a new report. This gate is STATUS-BLIND: it reads the ledger and the forwarded handle, never the status value, so DONE, NEEDS_NEXT, a stopped-run report (BLOCKED or NEEDS_CONTEXT), an out-of-enum value, and a turn with NO machine-readable status at all are ALL gated alike. BLOCKED and NEEDS_CONTEXT were an unconditional pass until a harness permission denial on the allocator give-back verb turned that door into a silent unowned leak; being unable to RELEASE is not being unable to NAME A CATCHER, and forwarding the handle is text in the dispatch's own fence - no tool, no permission, no live process - so the tightening traps nobody. Its sibling permission-denied-teardown.sh is what tells a dispatch this, at the moment its give-back verb is refused. Main-context / orchestrator-owned leases are NOT hard-gated, they are reclaimed by the SessionEnd gc backstop, which reclaims only the ENDING session's own running leases once its session anchor process is gone (`gc --scope anchor`, refused by the allocator while that anchor lives) plus leases whose owner is provably dead (`gc --scope dead-sessions`) - never the TTL arm, never another live session's lease, never a parked one; (2) enforce-grounding.sh's OSM-grounding-lie gate, which fires once when a subagent's artifact CLAIMS OSM grounding but its transcript shows zero OSM tool calls (self-gating; silently approves any non-Odoo-shaped subagent - see the script's own header); and (3) enforce-background-wait.sh's unwakeable-wait gate, which refuses a SUBAGENT stop while the payload's session-wide `background_tasks` array still lists, with `status: running`, either a `type: shell` entry whose task id the SUBAGENT'S OWN `agent_transcript_path` shows the Bash tool handing it, or - only on an unattended surface (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, or that variable unset with CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli) - a `type: subagent` entry whose id that same transcript shows an async Agent launch receipt naming. That gate never fires on main (the root is notified of every completion), never on the stopping subagent's own entry, and never on a `type: subagent` entry on an interactive or unknown surface (a stopped subagent is woken there by its child) - it exists because the Bash tool's own "you will be notified when it completes" line is written for the root and does not hold for a dispatched agent, whose SubagentStop IS the end of its dispatch, and because on an unattended surface a subagent that ends its turn after an async launch is never woken, so its child's result goes to the main session instead; its own header states the residuals, chiefly a command backgrounded outside the Bash tool (a bare `&`, `setsid`, `nohup`), which never becomes a task id and is invisible to it. The browser-family alternation (chrome-devtools|playwright|pagecast, each optionally -headed) in the PermissionRequest matcher and in the capture gate's PreToolUse matcher is a JSON-literal mirror of scripts/lib/browser_prefixes.py STATIC_SERVERS / scripts/lib/browser_mcp_servers.py ALL_SERVERS (JSON cannot import either file) - keep the four lists in sync when a browser family is added or removed (V-19). A separate PermissionRequest entry, matcher-scoped to mcp__plugin_odoo-ai-agents_odoo-local__.* (a JSON-literal mirror of scripts/lib/plugin_mcp_servers.py LOCAL_SERVERS), runs auto-approve-local.sh: it auto-allows every odoo-local tool (lease/instance/catalog) except lease_gc called with dry_run:false, which it leaves to the normal human prompt so an APPLY-mode reclaim - the one call in this surface that can actually stop a process group and drop a database - is never silently rubber-stamped; that PermissionRequest matcher also overlaps the browser one above (both fire on any mcp__plugin_odoo-ai-agents_ tool), which is harmless because auto-approve-browser.sh's own SSOT (browser_prefixes.py) excludes LOCAL_SERVERS and stays silent for an odoo-local tool. permission-denied-teardown.sh's PermissionDenied registration gained a second matcher-scoped entry, mcp__plugin_odoo-ai-agents_odoo-local__lease_(release|park), alongside its original Bash one - the same script branches on tool_name so a refused MCP lease give-back gets the identical forward-INSTANCE_HANDLE advice as a refused CLI one.
